items.title: Promise Robotics partners with D.R. Horton on physical AI for homebuilding - The Robot Report
items.summary: Promise Robotics said its technology interprets existing home designs, generates production plans and robotic instructions, orchestrates manufacturing, and connects that production with site installation. Rather than automating isolated tasks, the company said it brings these capabilities together in one integrated environment. [...] Promise Robotics is not a vertically integrated developer or a home designer like Reframe Systems, Attar acknowledged. “We’re more about the advancements in robotics, and we’re here to scale when companies need to scale,” he said. [...] “At D.R. Horton, we are always looking for innovations that can help us improve how we build. We are continuously focused on improving cycle times, increasing production capacity, and bringing greater consistency and predictability to our operations,” said Brad Conlon, senior vice president for strategic growth and innovation at D.R. Horton. “Promise Robotics’ integrated platform gives us a new capability to support those goals.”

items.title: Recent advances in AI are creating a 'paradigm shift' for robotics - Berkeley News
items.summary:
Traditionally, engineers can directly program the software that tells robots how to perceive objects, plan movements and control their actions, a process called model-based robotics. Or, with model-free robotics, they can train robots to learn behaviors from demonstrations through imitation learning. The first approach requires extensive engineering, while the second needs enormous amounts of data and time. [...] Berkeley-based Ambi Robotics, which specializes in logistics and warehouse order fulfillment, applied the new methods earlier this year to analyze parcel sorting data and test updates to robot behavior. Tests showed an increased capacity of over 15,000 packages sorted annually per robot; the change is now deployed across 30% of the company’s U.S. fleet. [...] Ken Goldberg

“Agentic robotics is a fundamental shift in how robots are controlled,” Goldberg said. “Instead of collecting massive amounts of data and hand-tuning every behavior, teams of agents can quickly generate, test and refine robot programs that allow human engineers to interpret how the programs work for fine-tuning and verification.”

items.title: Gemini Robotics Embodied Reasoning 2 is now available on Google Cloud | Google Cloud Blog
items.summary: Earlier this year, we introduced Gemini Robotics 2 — our next-generation intelligence layer enabling robots to think, act, and adapt in the physical world. At the core of this breakthrough is Gemini Robotics Embodied Reasoning 2 (ER 2), a specialized Gemini model that serves as a robot’s high-level brain. Working across any robot embodiment — from stationary arms to full humanoids — Gemini Robotics ER 2 combines advanced spatial and temporal video understanding with long-horizon planning and [...] Gemini Robotics ER 2 transforms a robot into a physical agent. The model combines deep spatio-temporal reasoning and long-horizon planning, enabling robots to orchestrate steps to complete a task, self-correct, and generalize to novel situations. To build an agentic setup, developers can declare low-level control interfaces — like Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models or navigation APIs — as tools, and stream multimodal video, audio, or text directly into the model. [...] Today, we are bringing this same frontier embodied reasoning model to enterprise production environments: Gemini Robotics ER 2 is now available in public preview on the Gemini platform. For the first time, organizations can pair Google DeepMind’s latest embodied reasoning model for robotics with the enterprise-grade security, multi-agent orchestration, and end-to-end lifecycle management of Google Cloud — making it easier to simulate, evaluate, and deploy safe, adaptive physical AI at scale.

items.title: Serve Robotics launches new business to become the AWS for robots | TechCrunch
items.summary:
Serve Robotics, a maker of self-driving sidewalk delivery robots, is expanding beyond its autonomous delivery operations in a bid to become a technology supplier to other companies building robots.

The company, which spun out of Uber’s acquisition of Postmates in 2021 and went public in 2024, said Thursday it will launch a new business line called Physical AI Services. [...] Specifically, Serve Robotics will offer customers its connectivity and data tools. Bedrock Robotics, a startup developing self-driving systems for construction equipment, is a customer, according to Serve. It’s also working with T-Mobile to bring AI computing power closer to robots, Serve announced alongside its third-quarter earnings on Thursday.

“We are solving the problem of robots in human spaces,” Serve Robotics CEO and co-founder Ai Kashani told TechCrunch. [...] Serve Robotics already makes two kinds of robots, the cute googly-eyed sidewalk delivery robot and one designed for hospitals that it got through its acquisition of Diligent Robotics.

Those businesses are not going away, Kashani emphasized in a recent interview. Instead, he said there is opportunity to sell the technology it developed for its own robots to other companies developing robots for farms, warehouses, and other uncontrolled environments.

items.title: Agility Robotics begins trading on Nasdaq
items.summary: “Congratulations to the entire Agility Robotics team on this incredible milestone,” said Nicolaus Radford, co-founder and CEO of humanoid startup Persona AI. “At a time when robotics headlines are too often dominated by hype and flashy demonstrations, Agility has focused on the hard work of putting robots to work. Built on a decade of engineering breakthroughs, relentless persistence and real-world deployments, Jonathan and his team have helped turn the promise of humanoid robotics into a [...] Agility Robotics, which spun out of Oregon State University in 2015, makes the Digit humanoid, which has been moving totes in warehouses. The company claimed that Digit has already logged more than 65,000 hours of operation across nine customer facilities. Customers include AGCO, GXO Logistics, Schaeffler, Mercado Libre, and Toyota Motor Manufacturing Canada. [...] “Today marks an important milestone for Agility, but the bigger story is what it means for the future of work,” stated Peggy Johnson, CEO of Agility Robotics. “AI is moving beyond the digital world and into the physical world, creating new possibilities for how people and machines work together. At Agility, that future is already taking shape.”
